summary: Coos County lookout: a 1942 Aircraft Warning Service post, staffed into 1958, abandoned in 1965 when the land and house went back to Weyerhaeuser; now gone, no site description found.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: firelookout.com gives a two-story house for 1942; the September 1942 letter describes a 14x14 Aladdin building waiting on slash cleanup. The sources do not say whether these are one building, so the story reports both without choosing.

notes_for_editor: The 1949 items name the agency two ways: the July 23 item says Coos Forest Protective association and the July 26 funeral notice says Coos Fire Protective association. The story uses the funeral notice's name for the lookout charge. The 1929 date appears only on firelookout.com; the Forest Lookouts page does not mention it. Mrs. Allen's initials differ across the 1957 and 1958 items (C.B., C.E., C.F.), so the story says only Mrs. Allen. The bare 'Removed' label on the Forest Lookouts page is not used. Two WebSearch queries surfaced no Vaughn Point record beyond a map listing; the offbeatoregon.com AWS article is general history and is not cited. Unread leads: a Bill McCash article in Waterways (Coos County Historical Society, September 2007), and Oregon State Archives record APD/25/224, a June 1942 AWS circular.
